courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Sport Performance
courses.description: Investigation of current theoretical perspectives, research, and applications of theory and techniques related to the field of sport psychology. Exploration of research as related to optimal performance in athletics and in life. Includes the history and foundations of sport and exercise psychology, the role of race, ethnicity, and gender in sport, personality, attribution and cognition, leadership, motivation, goal-setting, neuropsychology and physiology of arousal, attention, and the field of psychological skills training (PST) in sport, with potential applications in other performance-driven disciplines.

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
courses.instructor: Jim W. Stevens, Paul J. Brogan, Dale K. Hancock, Edward J. Abbasi, Rusty N. Stivers, Zeb Brayton
courses.description: Fundamental concepts concerning the interaction of biological and mechanical aspects of the musculoskeletal and neuromuscular structures. This course combines anatomy and kinesiology by addressing the anatomical structure and function of the musculoskeletal system as it relates to human movement and exercise. Muscular analysis and practical application, including strengthening and flexibility exercises for each muscle, will be emphasized. Students will also study physiological and biomechanical principles. Emphasis on the importance of the sub-disciplines such as; motor learning, motor development, biomechanics, exercise physiology, nutrition, and sports psychology in Kinesiology will be discussed along with career opportunities in the areas of teaching, coaching, allied health, and fitness professions.

courses.title: Global Health
courses.description: Introduces the growing field of global health, global health challenges, programs, and policies through theoretical foundations and research methods. Students will explore how health, illness, and well-being are shaped by social, cultural, political, economic, and environmental forces worldwide. Topics include comparative health systems; emerging global health priorities; social determinants of health; health systems reform; and major global health initiatives for disease prevention and health promotion. An emphasis is placed on global health ethics, health inequities, and issues of social justice.

Health disparities and inequities in sexually diverse, gender, racial, and minority populations will be explored, and culturally competent ideas to bridge the health equity gap and improve population health will be developed. courses.title: Critical Reading
courses.instructor: Christopher R. Briggs, Sarah B. Hawes
courses.description: This course offers students the opportunity to develop, evaluate, and apply critical reading skills and strategies. These strategies include annotating text, separating fact from opinion, analyzing supporting evidence, identifying propaganda techniques and logical fallacies, etc. Students apply attentive, rhetorical, and argumentative reading strategies to a variety of texts. Additional course topics include main ideas, inferred ideas, tone, style, and rhetorical strategies. A minimum of 5,000 words of writing is required. Formal writing includes rhetorical précis and analyses, critical responses, and an argumentative research paper; informal writing includes reading responses, learning reflections, essay drafts, and peer feedback.

Such questions can be answered with the basics of logical reasoning, including the deconstruction and evaluation of arguments, the structure of logic, and how to assess conclusions using various reasoning methodologies. Topics will include categorical syllogistic logic, propositional logic, and predicate logic which ultimately enable students to assess the strength of arguments in daily life and academic settings. CSCI 203 is cross-listed with PHILO 103.

courses.title: Ethics: Theory and Application
courses.description: What should I do with my life? What kind of person should I be? What makes actions right or wrong, good or bad? Is there any reason to be moral? Is morality subjective? How, if at all, can such questions be answered? These basic questions and themes will be examined through the study of historical and contemporary philosophical texts from key philosophical standpoints in ethics, emphasizing virtue ethics, utilitarianism, and deontology. These major as well as minor theories will be evaluated and applied in the critical context of personal as well as contemporary moral issues.

Methods will include unit conversions, measurement tolerances, accuracy, repeatability, ratios, and graphing. Course meets DAS Electrician Trainee and Journey Level Recertification CA State Requirements.
